chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, who said:

I entered upon Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام), and I asked him to write for me so that I might look at his handwriting and recognize it when it came. He said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'O Ahmad, handwriting may differ for you between the thick pen and the fine pen, so do not doubt.'

Then he called for the inkpot, and he wrote, and he kept drawing ink from the inkpot's channel. I said to myself while he was writing: 'I will ask him to gift me the pen with which he wrote.' When he finished writing, he turned to speak with me while wiping the pen with the cloth of the inkpot for a while. Then he said: 'Take it, O Ahmad,' and he handed it to me. I said: 'May I be your ransom, I am distressed by something affecting me within myself, and I had wanted to ask your father, but that was not decreed for me.' He said: 'And what is it, O Ahmad?'

I said: 'O my master, it has been narrated to us from your forefathers that the sleep of the Prophets is upon their backs, the sleep of the believers is upon their right sides, the sleep of the hypocrites is upon their left sides, and the sleep of the devils is upon their faces.' He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is so.'

I said: 'O my master, I strive to sleep on my right side, but I am unable, and sleep does not come to me upon it.' He remained silent for a while, then said: 'O Ahmad, come near me.' So I came near him. He said: 'Put your hand beneath your clothes.' So I put it in. Then he brought out his hand from beneath his clothes and inserted it beneath my clothes, and he wiped with his right hand over my left side and with his left hand over my right side three times.
Ahmad said: 'Since he (عليه السلام) did that to me, I have not been able to sleep on my left side, and sleep does not come to me upon it at all.'

key_terms.الدَّوَاةِ: the inkpot from which ink was drawn while writing
key_terms.الشَّيَاطِينِ: the devils, whose sleep is described as being upon their faces
key_terms.الْخَطَّ: handwriting; the written script whose variation the Imam explains
key_terms.الْقَلَمِ: the pen used for writing, mentioned in both thick and fine forms
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers, whose sleep is described as being upon their right sides
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِينَ: the hypocrites, whose sleep is described as being upon their left sides
key_terms.نَوْمَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the sleep of the Prophets, described here as being upon their backs
key_terms.يَمِينِي: my right side, the side on which Ahmad wished to sleep

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the sleeping positions of the Prophets, believers, hypocrites, and devils?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates Ahmad ibn Ishaq's meeting with Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (عليه السلام), in which the Imam first clarifies that handwriting can vary depending on the pen and then responds to Ahmad's concern about sleeping posture. The report affirms a transmitted distinction between the sleeping positions of Prophets, believers, hypocrites, and devils, and concludes with the Imam (عليه السلام) physically treating Ahmad so that he thereafter could no longer sleep on his left side.
